verses.text: My brothers and sisters, as you believe in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, don’t show favoritism.
Suppose someone enters your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and a poor person in shabby clothes comes in too.
If you give special attention to the person in fine clothes and say, “Here, have this good seat,” but tell the poor person, “Stand over there,” or “Sit on the floor by my feet,”
haven’t you made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
Listen, my dear brothers and sisters: didn’t God choose those who are poor in the eyes of the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom he promised to those who love him?
But you’ve dishonored the poor. Aren’t the rich the ones who oppress you and drag you into court?
Don’t they insult the honorable name you bear?
If you really fulfill the royal law found in Scripture, “Love your neighbor as yourself,” you’re doing well.
But if you show favoritism, you’re sinning and the law convicts you as lawbreakers.
Whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one point is guilty of breaking all of it.
For the one who said, “Don’t commit adultery,” also said, “Don’t murder.” If you don’t commit adultery but do murder, you’ve become a lawbreaker.
Speak and act as people who will be judged by the law that gives freedom.
Judgment without mercy will come to anyone who hasn’t shown mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.
My brothers and sisters, what good is it if someone claims to have faith but doesn’t act on it? Can that kind of faith save them?
Suppose a brother or sister has no clothes and no food for the day.
If one of you says, “Go in peace; stay warm and eat well,” but doesn’t give what their body needs, what good is that?
In the same way, faith by itself, if it doesn’t lead to action, is dead.
Someone might say, “You have faith and I have actions.” Show me your faith without actions, and I’ll show you my faith by what I do.
You believe there’s one God. Good! Even the demons believe that—and shudder.
You foolish person, do you need proof that faith without actions is useless?
Wasn’t Abraham our father shown to be righteous by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?
You see that faith was working together with his actions, and his faith was made complete by what he did.
That fulfilled the Scripture that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called God’s friend.
You see, a person is shown to be righteous by actions and not by faith alone.
In the same way, wasn’t Rahab the prostitute shown to be righteous by what she did when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out another way?
Just as a body without the spirit is dead, so faith without actions is dead.
